claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` claims to drop diagnostics about metadata members, but it only drops diagnostics that have a source location in another compilation. For a member of a PE-referenced type, the new `FirstOrDefault()` / `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` calls return null, so `Diagnostic.Create` gets `Location.None`. `Location.None.IsInSource` is false, so the guard `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || ...` passes and the diagnostic is reported. Concrete input: `lib` (built without the MessagePack analyzer, e.g. analyzer assets excluded, F#, or an older package) declares `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> { [Key(0)] public string Key {get;set;} public int Unkeyed {get;set;} }`; `app` uses `Item<int>` as a keyed member. On base this crashed. On head the consuming assembly gets a location-less MsgPack004 (an Error, L2) about a type it does not own. The same applies to MsgPack003/BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and other Location.None reports. This contradicts L8 (the defining assembly owns validating its own types) and breaks the app build instead of producing a clean one.

claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only drops diagnostics whose Location is in source but belongs to another compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None (metadata/null location, e.g. from FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() returning null) have IsInSource false and are still reported. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 (an Error per L2) for a member lacking [Key] is now emitted with no location in the user's build. Previously the type would crash; now a metadata type that lacks keys could fail the user's build with a location-less error, contradicting L8 (referenced types are deliberately not analysed).

claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose source tree is not in the current compilation, and the wrapper is installed for all diagnostics. Diagnostics for metadata members are now silently suppressed rather than prevented. The ledger (L8) says missing diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are not defects, so this is probably fine. The remaining risk is a diagnostic that protects users from an insecure configuration, such as MsgPack007/008 or a custom-formatter misuse, being dropped if its location is in a tree from another compilation. That is unlikely, because such locations come from the compilation's own syntax. No concrete security regression was found.
